clue.text: Hurried activity of the French after break

indicators.note: after places the French word behind the word for break

parts.note: to bust something is to break it
le is the French masculine form of 'the'

explanation.surface: Someone describes a flurry of French activity once a pause is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Bustle is noisy, energetic busyness, a synonym for hurried activity.

clue.text: Primate, president and a bishop coming in through

parts.note: Bush, surname of two US presidents

indicators.note: coming in says the a-and-bishop letters enter the word for through

parts.note: by can mean through, as in 'by way of'
B is the chess abbreviation for bishop

explanation.surface: A list of dignitaries: a primate, a president and a bishop arriving together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Primate' looks like an archbishop beside the president and bishop, but it is the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A bushbaby is a small nocturnal African primate, also called a galago.

clue.text: Sacred text giving some of Elisha's travels

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A holy book recounting part of the prophet Elisha's journeys.
explanation.definitionFit: A shastra is a Hindu scripture or treatise, so a sacred text.

clue.text: Port delays with nothing given entrance

indicators.note: given entrance says the zero is let into the word for delays

parts.note: lags means falls behind or delays
O, the figure zero, means nothing

explanation.surface: A harbour where hold-ups vanish once ships are allowed in.
explanation.definitionFit: Lagos is Nigeria's chief seaport on the Gulf of Guinea.

clue.text: Odds against you capturing map that might provide enemy location

indicators.note: against means beside, so the odds sit next to what follows

parts.note: SP, starting price, is the betting odds at the off

indicators.note: capturing says the word for you holds the word for map

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
a plan is a map or diagram

explanation.surface: A gambler weighs the odds against someone who has got hold of a map of enemy positions.
explanation.walkthrough: SP (starting price) is betting jargon for the odds; YE is archaic 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: A reconnaissance aircraft photographs territory, so it may reveal where the enemy is.

clue.text: Rex pallid and Rob turning a bright colour

indicators.note: turning says these letters are rotated into a new order

explanation.surface: Two men, a pale Rex and Rob, flush scarlet.
explanation.walkthrough: A pillar box is the tall red British post box, which gives the shade its name.
explanation.definitionFit: This vivid red shade is named after the traditional British post box.

clue.text: Nightingale is in a poem beginning with heart ill — roughly!

indicators.note: roughly says the gathered letters are rearranged loosely
beginning with takes only the opening letter of heart

explanation.surface: A poem about a nightingale starts with an ailing heart.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth Philomela was turned into a nightingale, so poets use her name for the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Philomela is a poetic name for the nightingale, from the Greek myth of her transformation.

clue.text: Applauds a daughter and son getting round difficult situation

indicators.note: getting round says the three letters surround the word for difficult situation

parts.note: a mire is a bog, figuratively a difficult situation

explanation.surface: Someone praises a daughter and son for overcoming a tough spot.
explanation.definitionFit: To admire someone is to regard them with approval, much like applauding them.

clue.text: Male ruler requiring comfortable home

parts.note: a nest is a snug, comfortable home

explanation.surface: A male monarch insists on a cosy place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: ER (Elizabeth Regina) is the standard crossword ruler.
explanation.definitionFit: Ernest is a man's first name, so it names a male.

clue.text: Spray reserve item good for storing

indicators.note: storing says the reserve item keeps the abbreviation inside it

parts.note: a spare is an extra kept in reserve

explanation.surface: A spare spray nozzle is a good thing to keep in storage.
explanation.definitionFit: To sparge is to sprinkle or spray, used of brewing with hot water.

clue.text: Spooner's constructed scheme for Highlander

indicators.note: Spooner's says the opening sounds of the two words change places

explanation.surface: A Highlander devises a building plan in the manner of the famous tongue-twisting don.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds gives 'plade man'; in Scotland 'plaid' is said to rhyme with 'made'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Highlander wears tartan plaid, so is jocularly a man in a plaid.

clue.text: I sense Scot is possibly an SNP type?

indicators.note: possibly says these letters may be arranged otherwise

explanation.surface: A speaker senses a Scot may be a nationalist party member.
explanation.walkthrough: The SNP is the Scottish National Party, which campaigns for Scottish independence from the UK.
explanation.definitionFit: SNP members want Scotland to leave the UK, so each is one who favours breaking away.

clue.text: David's wife, university arts graduate penning novel

indicators.note: penning says the graduate's credentials enclose the novel's title

parts.note: Bath is an English university town and university
She is H. Rider Haggard's novel

explanation.surface: A biblical wife is pictured as a graduate who writes fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like an adjective but names H. Rider Haggard's adventure story; Bath is a university city in the west of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Bathsheba was the wife of King David in the Old Testament.

clue.text: Plant right in the middle of round river island

indicators.note: in the middle of puts the letter for right inside the other pieces

explanation.surface: A plant sits squarely in the centre of a round island in a river.
explanation.definitionFit: Orris is the iris whose fragrant root is used in perfume.

clue.text: A stabber seen to reform and show remorse

indicators.note: reform says the letters are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A knifeman is observed turning over a new leaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Beating one's breast is an idiom for public displays of guilt or regret.

clue.text: Decorations consisting of yellow tags round holy books

parts.note: or is gold or yellow in heraldry

indicators.note: round says the word for tags wraps the holy books

explanation.surface: Golden name tags are hung around Bibles as decoration.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornaments are decorative objects, synonymous with decorations.

clue.text: Small bits of substance smuggled aboard ship

indicators.note: smuggled aboard says the substance is carried inside the ship

explanation.surface: Contraband in small quantities is sneaked onto a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A smatter is a slight, scrappy amount, so smatters are small bits.

clue.text: Extra-slim Susan transformed in what may amount to a denial of femininity?

definitions.text: what may amount to a denial of femininity

indicators.note: transformed says these letters change shape into a new word

explanation.surface: A very thin woman named Susan undergoes a change of body image.
explanation.definitionFit: This identity rejects the sex assigned at birth, which may involve rejecting being female.

clue.text: Acted like a pig let loose in area of land

indicators.note: this word is a container marker: it says one piece is placed inside the other, and the clue words of the pieces show which way round

parts.note: a rood is an old measure of land, a quarter acre

indicators.note: loose says the three letters are set free into a new order

explanation.surface: A pig is turned loose in a field.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Acted like a pig' reads as an insult, but it literally means nosing about in soil; the scrambled letters sit inside an old quarter-acre measure.
explanation.definitionFit: To rootle is to dig with the snout, as a pig does when foraging.

clue.text: Hardening within university clique

parts.note: a ring is a closed group or clique

explanation.surface: Toughening up within a university's exclusive set.
explanation.definitionFit: Inuring means accustoming to hardship, toughening someone so they cope.

clue.text: Spider in gym, one descending in time

indicators.note: in says the gym letters and numeral go inside the word for time

parts.note: an era is a period of time

indicators.note: descending, in a down clue, puts the numeral below the gym letters

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A spider in the gym is seen lowering itself in due course.
explanation.walkthrough: PE is school gym class; EPEIRA is an orb-weaving spider genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Epeira is a genus of orb-weaving spiders, the garden spider among them.

clue.text: Like sort of tournament or concert in which ace appears

indicators.note: in which says the card letter sits inside the concert

parts.note: a prom is a promenade concert

explanation.surface: A star player turns up at a tournament or a concert.
explanation.walkthrough: The Proms are a London summer season of classical concerts.
explanation.definitionFit: A pro-am golf event pairs professionals with amateurs.

clue.text: Believe too much, open to corruption

explanation.surface: A credulous person is too trusting and liable to be corrupted.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtrust is to place excessive faith, believing someone more than is wise.

clue.text: Japanese sword guard shown up in a piece of sculpture

indicators.note: shown up, in a down clue, means read from bottom to top

parts.note: a bust is a sculpted head and shoulders

explanation.surface: A Japanese sword guard is displayed in a sculpture.
explanation.definitionFit: A tsuba is the metal handguard on a Japanese sword such as a katana.

clue.text: One leader beset by misfortunes is in a state

indicators.note: beset by says the numeral and leader are surrounded by misfortunes

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
No 1, number one, is the leader

explanation.surface: A leader plagued by troubles is in a bad state.
explanation.definitionFit: Illinois is a midwestern US state.

clue.text: Like some ferocious beast left inert, head hidden

indicators.note: head hidden says the first letter of the word for inert is taken away

explanation.surface: A fierce animal lies motionless with its head out of sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Lupine means wolf-like, and the wolf is a fierce predator.

clue.text: Rock from volcano to the west around side that's molten

indicators.note: around says the turned volcano surrounds the remade letters
to the west, in an across clue, reads the volcano right to left
molten says these letters are melted down and recast

explanation.surface: Lava flowing west round the flank of a volcano.
explanation.walkthrough: In an across clue 'to the west' means read leftwards; 'that's molten' rearranges the side word, fitting the lava picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Andesite is a volcanic rock named after the Andes.

clue.text: Groups of workers crossing English river

indicators.note: crossing says the groups straddle the abbreviation

explanation.surface: Work gangs ford an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ganges is India's great sacred river.
